title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in Corollary III (§72, previous page) Euler set A=0 in his earlier general quartic result. This gives an algebraic integral of dx/√(x(B+Cx+Dx²+Ex³)) ± dy/√(…)=0. Substituting x→x², y→y² turns it into an integral of dx/√X ± dy/√Y = 0 with X = B+Cx²+Dx⁴+Ex⁶. This page starts the 'Analysis' that rederives that integral by Lagrange's mechanical method.

§73. Introduce a 'time' t with dx/√X = dt, so dy/√Y = ∓dt. Squaring gives (dx/dt)² = X and (dy/dt)² = Y. Multiply by x² and y² respectively. New variables: p = (x²+y²)/2 and q = (x²−y²)/2, so dp = x dx + y dy and dq = x dx − y dy. Then dp·dq = x²dx² − y²dy², hence dp dq/dt² = x²X − y²Y. Divide by 2q = x²−y² to get a divided difference:
(x²X−y²Y)/(x²−y²) = B + C(x²+y²) + D(x⁴+x²y²+y⁴) + E(x²+y²)(x⁴+y⁴).
In p, q this is B + 2Cp + D(3p²+q²) + 4E(p³+pq²).

§'64' (a misprint for §74). With dt constant, differentiating (dx/dt)² = X gives 2ddx/dt² = X' (X' = dX/dx), and likewise for y. Multiply by x and add 2dx²/dt² = 2X to get 2d(x dx)/dt² = xX' + 2X; similarly for y (next page). Summing gives a second-order equation for p. Subtracting 4× the first-order relation leaves 2ddp/dt² − 2dp dq/(q dt²) = 8Dq² + 32Epq². Multiplying by dp/q² makes it exact, giving (dp/dt)²/q² = 4Δ + 8Dp + 16Ep². In x, y this is (x√X ∓ y√Y)/(x²−y²) = √(Δ + D(x²+y²) + E(x²+y²)²): the algebraic integral, with Δ the constant of integration.

The whole page is a direct transposition of Lagrange's 1766–69 'mechanical' trick (p = x+y, q = x−y, t as time) to squared variables. This handles an even sextic whose differential is really an elliptic differential in u = x².
errors: Typographical: 'Ex priore fit 2xddx/dt = xX'' — the denominator should be dt², as the following line makes clear.
In the header of §74 the expressions 'aequationes dx²/dt² et dy²/dt²' are elliptical (meaning dx²/dt² = X, dy²/dt² = Y); there is no mathematical error.
All algebra checked. x²+y² = 2p; x⁴+x²y²+y⁴ = 3p²+q²; x⁶+x⁴y²+x²y⁴+y⁶ = 4p(p²+q²). So B+2Cp+D(3pp+qq)+4E(p³+pqq) is correct, as is dp dq = x²dx² − y²dy².

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary time t and treating the separated differential equation as a dynamical system, then forming sum/difference variables to obtain a second-order equation with an obvious first integral
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's method for the Euler addition theorem (mechanical/Hamiltonian-style derivation of the elliptic addition law)
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop., Opera Omnia I.21); Euler also comments on Lagrange's method in Institutiones calculi integralis supplements/related papers (unsure of exact locations)

ideas.what: Applying the method to the even sextic B+Cx²+Dx⁴+Ex⁶ using p=(x²+y²)/2, q=(x²−y²)/2
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of a hyperelliptic (genus-2, even sextic) differential to an elliptic one via u=x²; addition theorem transported along the quotient map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Reduction of even-sextic hyperelliptic integrals usually associated with Legendre/Jacobi; the substitution itself is elementary and goes back to Euler

ideas.what: Division of x²X − y²Y by x² − y² (divided difference) expressed symmetrically in p, q

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct, routine adaptation of Lagrange's well-known method to an even sextic, which is really the elliptic case in u = x². E506 is published in the Opera omnia and this content is part of it. Nothing new beyond two misprints.
transcription_corrections: '§. 64' as printed is a misprint for '§. 74'.
'2xddx/dt = xX'' in the print should read 2xddx/dt² = xX'.
In the §74 heading the image shows garbled 'd x²/d t²' notation; it means the equations dx²/dt² = X and dy²/dt² = Y.
